subject: MATHEMATICS
applicability_conditions: learner must use the fact that a point on an axis has one coordinate equal to zero
use when an intercept or an axis-constrained point is guessed from a picture instead of derived
anchor: Lying on an axis is an algebraic constraint: on the y-axis x = 0 and on the x-axis y = 0, which turns a two-variable problem into one unknown.
ordinary_language_bridge: Ask 'which coordinate is forced to zero here?' and write that equation down before solving anything.
reconstruction_route: state which axis the unknown point lies on
write the forced coordinate as an explicit equation
substitute the constraint into the given relation or distance condition
write the answer back as an ordered pair
check the pair against both the constraint and the original condition

minimal_contrast.shared_structure: the same line or the same pair of reference points
minimal_contrast.prediction_prompt: Which substitution answers the question that was actually asked?
minimal_contrast.decisive_feature: the named axis fixes which coordinate is zero, independent of which looks easier

misconception_discriminator.candidate_wrong_model: an intercept is read off a sketch or taken as the constant term of any written form
misconception_discriminator.probe: give a relation not in slope-intercept form and ask for the y-axis crossing with a check
misconception_discriminator.decisive_response: learner substitutes x = 0 and verifies the resulting pair in the original relation

repair_route: re-state the axis membership as an equation
substitute and solve for the single remaining unknown
write and verify the ordered pair
verification_method: substitute the found pair into the original relation or distance condition
confirm the forced coordinate is exactly zero in the reported pair
known_limitations: does not decide whether an intercept exists for a degenerate relation
does not replace distance-formula competence in equidistance problems
